verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The two constraints, the weights R^2 and R, the components used (u.mean.angular = v, u.mean.axial = γ, both components of the mean correction and not of the slow base, since `State.mean` is the triple added to `Context.base` in `State.totalVelocity`), and the inner average all match. ⟨·⟩_Y is `PressureStream.torusAverage`, the iterated unit-period integral ∫_0^1∫_0^1 over `Plane = ℝ × ℝ`, i.e. normalized Haar measure on the 2-torus; the paper introduces Y ∈ 𝕋² = ℝ²/ℤ² on p. 62, so the dimension and the normalization agree. One routine rewriting is needed: `pressureMass` integrates over all of ℝ (∫ r, …), not over [0,∞) as the paper's convention on p. 88 prescribes ("Unspecified radial integrals run from zero to infinity"). The two agree because the correction components are supported inside the active shell: `PressureStream.pressureMass_eq_interval` turns `pressureMass f s` into `∫ r in a..b, torusAverage f (r,s)` for any `RadialAlias.RadiallySupported a b` smooth f, and the paper's shell has 0 < a, so ∫_ℝ = ∫_a^b = ∫_0^∞ on these integrands. The second, cosmetic point: the Lean gives no separate names M_θ and M_z; the moments appear only inline as `radialMoment 2 u.mean.angular` and `radialMoment 1 u.mean.axial`. (These are not `CorrectionState.thetaDefect` / `axialDefect`, which carry the extra base and covariance terms and correspond to the defects 𝒥_θ, 𝒥_z of (8.12)/(8.15).) `ZeroMasses` is a global statement (equality of `ScalarField S`, so for every stage index n and every slow point); `ZeroMassesOn` is its restriction to a slow set, and `ZeroMassesOn.of_global` derives the latter from the former.
